title: Sharjah Airport Authority, Cycling Club sign partnership deal
article_text:
The agreement was signed by Ali Salim Al Midfa, Chairman of Sharjah Airport Authority, and Sheikh Rashid bin Saqr Al Qasimi, Chairman of the Club's Board of Directors, in the presence of Sheikh Faisal bin Saud Al Qasimi, Director of Sharjah Airport Authority, alongside representatives from both parties.

Spanning two years, the agreement includes the Authority’s support for races, championships, programmes and initiatives organised by the Club at local, regional and international levels.

It also provides for exploring opportunities to collaborate on sporting projects and events, and for establishing mechanisms for participation and support in line with both parties' objectives.

Ali Salim Al Midfa, Chairman of Sharjah Airport Authority, said that sport is a key pillar of the Authority’s commitment to the community, given its role in promoting healthy lifestyles and enhancing quality of life.

He added that the cooperation agreement with Sharjah Cycling Club builds on the Authority’s commitment to establishing strategic partnerships that support Sharjah’s sports sector and strengthen the emirate’s position as a distinguished destination for hosting sporting events and championships. In turn, this supports the tourism sector and increases travel activity.

Sheikh Rashid bin Saqr Al Qasimi, Chairman of Sharjah Cycling Club’s Board of Directors, expressed his deep appreciation for the initiative, commending the national and community-focused role played by Sharjah Airport Authority and its commitment to supporting sporting initiatives that enhance quality of life and promote a culture of sport and physical activity across the community.

He affirmed that the partnership would open new avenues for launching distinctive initiatives and programmes, helping to promote cycling, establish Sharjah as a leading regional hub for the sport, and deliver a sustainable positive impact on the community.

The agreement builds on Sharjah Airport Authority’s ongoing efforts to strengthen its partnerships with local institutions and support initiatives that serve the community and contribute to sustainable development across the emirate.

title: F1 sponsors focus on contract terms as average deals hit $8.1M
article_text:
F1 sponsors focus on contract terms as average deals hit $8.1M

Ampere Analysis forecasts that Formula 1 sponsorship spend will top $3 billion in 2026. The average F1 deal costs nearly four times the average NBA or NFL deal. Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire says the old advertising-value-equivalency math has been upended. He says brands should structure deals around their end goals rather than promises of exposure.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Sports & Entertainment teams put it to work with Events & Onsite Capture.

Ampere Analysis forecasts that F1 sponsorship spend will pass $3 billion in 2026, up 15% on last season and 66% since 2022. Business Insider's Lara O'Reilly reported those figures along with a harder question from the marketing chiefs writing the checks: with this many logos on the grid, what does any one of them actually buy?

The people closest to these deals keep pointing to the contract. That suggests the rights a brand negotiates could matter more than the exposure it gets.

The scale is both the problem and the pitch. F1 now has more than 400 sponsorship partners, an average of 34 per team, and the average deal costs nearly four times the average NBA or NFL deal. A buyer paying that premium shares the car, the kit and the paddock with dozens of other brands.

Business Insider cited a 2024 academic paper finding that sponsors were more likely to renew when their team performed well, and that a larger sponsor roster was linked to a higher chance that individual brands would leave. Tim Crow, a longtime sports-marketing consultant, said F1's huge global audience includes fewer passionate fans than football or NASCAR, so brands have to work harder to stand out.

The audience still explains why brands keep paying. F1 says its global fan base reached 827 million in 2025, up 12% on the prior season, and that 43% of fans are under 35 and 42% are women. Few properties offer that mix on a calendar that runs most of the year and crosses continents.

Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire told Business Insider he sees some brands overpaying for F1 rights, which makes the market messier for everyone else. His second point matters more to anyone building a measurement plan. The old advertising-value-equivalency math has been upended, he said.

Other big sports buyers are taking a closer look too. McDonald's recently said it would end a 32-year FIFA World Cup partnership, and Heineken said last year it would end its 30-year UEFA Champions League sponsorship in 2027. Neither is an F1 deal. Both show that long-running sponsorships now face the same review as any other large line item.

McGuire's advice is to structure the deal around the brand's end goals rather than promises of exposure, and Qualcomm's own renewal shows how that works. When Qualcomm renewed with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team earlier this year, McGuire pushed for a separate agreement with driver Kimi Antonelli. McGuire says F1 is delivering strong return for the company.

Ben Cronin, editor of SportBusiness Sponsorship, reported that the addition of Brazilian driver Rafael Câmara to Haas F1's driver lineup has unlocked a sponsorship deal with Bradesco, one of Brazil's largest banks. A driver's nationality and profile can open a market for the team and the sponsor at once. That makes the driver lineup a fair topic in any negotiation, not something to wait and see about.

In B2B deals the equivalent is hospitality. Misha Sher, founder of the talent-management and brand-marketing firm One of Not Many, explained the logic to Business Insider using Oracle's partnership with Red Bull. Oracle doesn't need 100 million viewers, he said. It needs 25 decision-makers to understand how it uses technology under extreme pressure.

For a B2B sponsor, the return on an average $8.1 million F1 deal could depend on who sits in the hospitality suite.

The categories growing fastest are the ones whose products can do a visible job for a team. Ampere reports that F1 sponsorship revenue from software companies has grown 65% since 2022 and 42% since 2025. Revenue from AI-native companies is up nearly 450% since last season. Sher said brands that show how their technology helps on track get the most traction, and he pointed to Oracle with Red Bull and to Google building its Pixel phones and Gemini into McLaren's work with drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

SponsorUnited, via Motorsport.com; Ampere Analysis, via Business Insider

Motorsport.com, citing SponsorUnited, puts 2025 team sponsorship at $2.54 billion, up 22% on the previous year.

Three teams have signed wellness partners this year, Alex Harrington of Motorsport.com reported. The products are aimed as much at mechanics and engineers as at drivers, and Eight Sleep designs its beds for long-haul travel and time-zone changes. Because a wellness brand sells something fans can buy for themselves, the bigger prize could sit outside the garage, in fan activations that turn a team deal into consumer sales.

The model doesn't fit every buyer. For brands outside technology and automotive-adjacent industries, Crow said the numbers can be hard to make work. Lego and LVMH are his examples of brands that got through anyway. Lego built drivable cars for the 2025 Miami Grand Prix and the 2026 British Grand Prix. LVMH makes custom Louis Vuitton trophy trunks and supplies the Moët & Chandon the winners spray on the podium. Both made objects that became part of the race weekend.

title: Rolex keeps time for Davis Cup through extension
article_text:
World Tennis, the recently rebranded global governing body, has extended its commercial tie-up with luxury Swiss watch brand Rolex.

Through a contract extension unveiled today, Rolex will continue as a sponsor of the Davis Cup men's national teams series; the brand will keep its designation as official timekeeper of that competition.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Rolex has been in that position since 2007, while its overall involvement in tennis dates back to 1978. GlobalData Sport has valued its most recent tie-up at $1.25 million annually.

It is now, in addition to its Davis Cup involvement, it is a partner of all four Grand Slam tournaments, a sponsor of both the men's ATP and women's WTA tours, and – in addition – the official timekeeper for the Finals of the women's Billie Jean King Cup.

It also has specific agreements in place with current tennis stars Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner.

This deal has been unveiled in the build-up to the Final 8 finale of the 2026 Davis Cup, which is taking place in Bologna, Italy, between November 24 (tomorrow) and 29.

This month has already seen Yonex, the Japanese racket sports equipment brand, named as the tennis ball partner for this year's Davis Cup Final 8.

The 2026 Davis Cup Final 8 will see eight national teams compete to be crowned world champions. Alongside hosts Italy, seven winning nations from September's second-round qualifiers will participate in the event, including Czechia, Canada, South Korea, Great Britain, Germany, Austria and Spain.

International insurance company Generali Group was recently named as the new presenting partner for the Davis Cup, meanwhile.

World Tennis' commercial portfolio for the tournament also includes the likes of Visa, MG, Corpay, Fred Perry, and Betsson.

Ross Hutchins, chief executive at World Tennis, commented: "The brand is synonymous with success and prestige, and their commitment to our competition is a source of great pride for us. This news is another highlight in a year of significant commercial growth in Davis Cup as we look forward to the Final 8 this week."

World Tennis was unveiled as a rebrand of the International Tennis Federation in late June.

Arnaud Boetsch, Rolex's director of communications and image, added: "Our continued partnership with the Davis Cup by Generali reflects a relationship developed over many years, and we are proud to support the tournament and its values of team spirit, passion and sporting tradition."

The Swiss watchmaker's stable of sporting tie-ups also includes a tie-up with North American golf's top-tier PGA Tour – that deal has also been extended this month.

It also has deals in place with properties including golf's DP World Tour and World Sailing.

title: UEFA awards media rights to club competitions in 10 markets
article_text:
UEFA, European soccer’s governing body, has awarded broadcast rights to its major club competitions in 10 markets across Europe, Oceania, and the Caribbean after announcing its preferred bidders for the 2027-31 cycle.

The markets covered in this process are Australia, the Caribbean, Cyprus, the Dominican Republic, Greece, Iceland, Israel, Malta, New Zealand, and Türkiye.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Rights have been awarded for the elite UEFA Champions League (UCL), secondary Europa League, and third-tier Conference League for the next four seasons, from 2027-28 through 2030-31.

The process, described as “highly competitive”, included incumbent broadcasters, new market entrants, global digital platforms as well as local pay and free-to-air channels. New partners were secured in five of the 10 markets.

In Australia, all UCL rights have been snapped up by international sports streaming giant DAZN, which includes Foxtel and Kayo Sports.

DAZN has also landed rights to all three club competitions in Israel.

Elsewhere in Europe, rights to all club competitions have been secured by free-to-air (FTA) broadcaster Skai in Greece, pay-TV operator Cyta in Cyprus (with public-service broadcaster CYBC to show UCL Tuesday first pick games on a co-exclusive basis), digital streaming platform Exxen in Turkey, and cable pay-TV broadcaster Melita in Malta, with the semi-finals and finals of each competition to be shown FTA by the government-owned public broadcaster PBS.

CYBC will now provide free coverage of the UCL in Cyprus after previously having rights to the Europa League and Conference League, while Exxen returns as the rightsholder in Turkey, taking over from public-service broadcaster TRT.

In Iceland, streaming service Viaplay will keep UCL rights, while OTT platform Livey has acquired the Europa League and Conference League.

In the Caribbean, CPSL has retained rights to the UCL, Europa League, and Conference League, with ATV having all rights in Suriname co-exclusively. CPSL’s deal also covers the Dominican Republic.

Broadcast partners for the Europa League and Conference League in Australia, and for all three competitions in New Zealand, have been awarded to a preferred bidder but will be announced at a later date.

As well as Viaplay and CPSL, the deals with CYTA, Melita and PBS are also renewals.

UEFA went to market in all 10 territories at the end of September, with a deadline for submissions of November 3.

The tender process was managed by the UC3 commercial arm, a joint venture between UEFA and the European Football Clubs' body, and Relevant Football partners, UEFA’s sales agency for the club competitions through 2033, spanning media, sponsorship, and licensing rights.

Sportcal (GlobalData Sport) understands Relevent’s third and final multi-market tender concluded with an average uplift of around 150% across the 10 markets, which represents the strongest result of the 2027-31 media rights cycle so far for the agency.

Just 12 months after Relevent opened the process with its tender for Europe's top five markets in late 2025, only a small number of markets remain to be finalised.

These are Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Gibraltar, the Indian Subcontinent, Montenegro, North Macedonia, the Pacific Islands, Serbia, Slovenia and Ukraine.

title: Liverpool swap Standard Chartered logo for Play On
article_text:
Liverpool’s men’s and women’s teams have replaced Standard Chartered’s front-of-shirt logo with the Play On message, using one of the most visible sponsorship assets in world sport to tackle girls dropping out of sport.

Liverpool Women wore the Play On shirts against Chelsea on 21st November, followed by the men’s team against Manchester United at Anfield on 22nd November. Before both fixtures, a giant 25m x 23m Play On shirt was displayed on the pitch at St Helens and Anfield.

The limited-edition match shirts are being signed and auctioned, with all proceeds from this year’s campaign going to LFC Foundation to fund programmes that help more girls stay in sport.

Standard Chartered also brought together organisations from across sport, business and civil society at Anfield to discuss how collective action can address the barriers girls face. Guests included representatives from UN Women, the International Working Group on Women and Sport, Liverpool FC and LFC Foundation.

Erica Kerner, Global Head of Brand Partnerships and Sponsorships at Standard Chartered, said, “Sport gives girls so much more than the opportunity to play. It can build confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership skills that can open doors throughout their lives. Yet girls still drop out of sport at twice the rate of boys by the age of 14. Through Play On, we’re leveraging the power and reach of our partnership with LFC to shine a light on this issue, connecting brands and organisations to create more opportunities for girls to fulfil their potential on and beyond the pitch.”

Kate Theobald, SVP of Global Partnerships at Liverpool FC, said, “Our long-standing partnership with Standard Chartered has always been about more than football, and Play On is a great example of how we can work together to make a meaningful difference. Since launching the initiative in 2023, we’ve continued to build on its impact, using the club’s global reach and the strength of our partnership to raise awareness of the barriers girls face in sport and encourage positive change.“

Theobald continues,“We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved together through Play On over the years, and particularly pleased that this year’s campaign will directly support LFC Foundation and its work to create more opportunities for girls to stay involved in sport. It’s another important step in our shared commitment to making a lasting difference.”

Launched in 2023, Play On is part of the London-headquartered bank’s wider sporting portfolio, which expanded last week when Standard Chartered became a Formula 1 Global Partner from 2027.

title: ITV lands Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 rights
article_text:
ITV will be the exclusive UK broadcaster of the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, with Birmingham’s own Alison Hammond and Paralympian Ade Adepitan co-hosting the opening and closing ceremonies.

The Games run from 10th to 17th July 2027 and will bring together 550 competitors from 26 nations across 12 adaptive sports, alongside 1,100 family members and supporters. A further 30,000 spectators are expected each day.

ITV’s free-to-air coverage will include both ceremonies, daily highlights programmes and exclusive digital content across ITVX, ITV YouTube and ITV’s social channels. Livewire Pictures will produce the host broadcast, covering all 12 sports and the ceremonies for audiences worldwide.

The deal was confirmed on ITV’s This Morning, where Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, appeared alongside former competitors Josh Boggi and Jules Bale. The appearance also marked key milestones in the build-up, including the launch of general sale tickets, volunteer recruitment and the growth of the INSPIRE education programme, which has now engaged nearly 50,000 young learners.

Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, Patron of the Invictus Games Foundation, said, “Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham was the place where so many of our competitors, who were critically wounded in Iraq and Afghanistan, woke up. So the first people they would see were the nurses and doctors in Queen Elizabeth Hospital. For them to come back with me and go back there was a really brilliant moving moment. Hundreds of British soldiers were treated at Queen Elizabeth Hospital. So for them to be going back to the Games in that city means a lot. I don’t think there’s a city in the UK that means so much to them. It’s the right place for it.”

Birmingham was chosen to host because of its long connection to the recovery and rehabilitation of the Armed Forces community. The city is home to Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham and the Royal Centre for Defence Medicine.

Katie Rawcliffe, Director of Entertainment, Reality & Daytime Commissioning at ITV, said, “The Invictus Games is such a beloved event and, we couldn’t be prouder at ITV to be the exclusive UK broadcaster. Our extensive coverage will extend across ITV, ITVX and ITV YouTube for our viewers to enjoy free-to-air, ensuring they do not miss a minute of the action.”

Vicky Gosling, Chair of Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, said, “Having ITV as our exclusive broadcast partner is a major milestone for Birmingham 2027. ITV’s commitment reflects the strength of the Invictus Games, the importance of the stories we have to tell and the appetite among UK audiences to hear them. Together, we can bring the recovery journeys of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans to millions of people, building understanding and support for the community at the heart of our Games.”

This news come after Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 confirmed the continuation of its partnership with Ottobock, which will provide technical support for competitors during the Games in the UK.

title: Meta inks 49ers sponsorship, will give away AI glasses
article_text:
The 49ers have signed Silicon Valley neighbor Meta to a sponsorship described by parties as a “landmark multiyear partnership,” which will emphasize the company’s high-end version of is A.I. glasses.

The newly created category for Meta is “official moment maker” of the 49ers. At launch, the signature activation will be a giveaway of Oakley Meta HSTN glasses to more than 4,700 49ers suite holders and club season ticket holders to celebrate the 80th anniversary of the franchise. Oakley, an NFL sponsor, typically sells the product at for $399 or more.

Also, Meta’s Whatsapp messenger app will become the “official instant messenger provider” of the 49ers, intended to support the team’s global marketing efforts in the U.K., UAE and Mexico in the NFL’s global markets program.

In a prepared statement, 49ers COO Brent Schoeb said “Innovation and technology are part of our franchise’s DNA,” making the connection logical. We ... look forward to seeing the content they create with Meta’s AI glasses.“ Financial terms were not disclosed.

Also, Meta will be the presenting sponsor of the 49ers’ military “Salute to Service” campaign, with a dedicated focus on blind and low-vision veterans. Meta will receive digital signage at Levi’s Stadium in the deal.

Meta has signed 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk as a brand ambassador to support the sponsorship.

Meta’s current sports sponsorship portfolio includes the UFC and Arsenal F.C. The team negotiated the deal with Meta directly.

title: Novo signs on as 76ers corporate sponsor
article_text:
Pharma giant Novo has signed on as a 76ers corporate sponsor. The parent company of weight-loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy gets presenting sponsorship of an online content series, along with social, digital and arena signage inventory. Additional activation will be through a “First Step Sweepstakes” in which fans can win Sixers experiences and merchandise by pledging to complete various healthy activities.

Outside of a pro cycling team, the drugmaker has been quiet in the U.S. with sports sponsorships, while its outsized media spend included a 90-second ad in the most recent Super Bowl.

Demark-based Novo has U.S. headquarters in Plainsboro, N.J., about 53 miles from the 76ers’ training facility and corporate HQ in Camden, N.J.

With manufacturing facilities and more than 2500 employees in North Carolina, Novo has been a Hurricanes sponsor since 2023. A year ago, it completed a deal with the Univ. of North Carolina which included branding on the Tar Heels’ home court. A recent rebrand of the corporate moniker from Novo Nordisk to Novo is another rationale for the Sixers sponsorship.

Meanwhile, with their resurgence, the 76ers have signed more than a dozen new sponsors out of a total count of 23.

“Their proximity and our commitment to heath and community brought this together,” said Owen Morin, the CRO of partnerships at Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment.

title: Why MLB could be the first major league to move its championship to streaming
article_text:
It's not a question of if, but when the first major American professional sports league puts its championship exclusively on a streaming service. Based on timing and the value of that championship, Major League Baseball is in the perfect position to make that decision, but only if it chooses.

Streaming services have quickly become major players in the American sports media rights space. Prime Video now has rights to the NFL, NBA, and NASCAR. Peacock is saturated with MLB, NBA, Premier League, and basketball and football from the Big Ten. Netflix has rights to MLB and NFL, and will exclusively air the 2027 Women's FIFA World Cup in the United States and Canada (and could soon secure rights to the 2030 men's World Cup).

But none of those rights include championship games, except Netflix and the Women's World Cup. The NFL, MLB, and NBA have gone as far as to put playoff games on streamers (the entirety of the 2027 NBA Eastern Conference Final will air on Prime Video), but the Big Four leagues have not gone all the way yet.

There is good reason to believe, however, that could soon change. Both the NHL and MLB will see their media rights expire after the 2028 season (if there is a lockout, the MLB contracts could go through 2029). Streamers have already shown interest in both leagues. NHL games air on ESPN Unlimited and Hulu, while MLB games stream across Netflix, Peacock, and Apple TV.

With the NFL and NBA locked into relatively longer contracts, based on timing alone, the league to make the streaming jump first for its championship could be the NHL or MLB.

The NHL's public comments have already tipped their hand; not necessarily that they are about to deal the Stanley Cup Final to a streamer, but that they are looking for a significant media rights increase, 50% to 100% more, according to CNBC. The NHL currently makes around $650 million annually from its U.S. media contracts.

While MLB has not indicated so publicly, the league will likely look for an increase in a similar range. That has been the norm in media rights recently. The NBA's latest contracts saw an increase more in the range of 150%.

One of the reasons the NBA was able to get such an increase is that the league was willing to put key inventory on streaming. Games on Peacock and Prime are key components of the NBA's agreement. As previously mentioned, both services air playoff games, and Prime goes as far as the conference finals.

The other key reason the NBA got its increase was competition. ESPN, Prime, NBC, and TNT were four media companies competing for three packages. Having more bidders than packages drove up the price for the NBA. If either league truly wants to maximize its next national deal, it needs to incentivize competition for its key media rights packages. Allowing streamers to bid on their championship inventory could be that incentive.

MLB has already carved out a streaming package of key rights for Netflix, featuring Opening Night, the Home Run Derby, and a special-event game. The league has shown a willingness to put important inventory on streaming already, which could signal a willingness to shop the World Series.

But why MLB instead of the NHL? MLB has more to gain because the World Series is more popular than the Stanley Cup Final. This year's World Series averaged 11.83 million viewers on Fox; the Stanley Cup Final averaged less than half that, 5.27 million viewers on ABC (which was the most-watched since 2019).

MLB has also historically been far more reliant on revenue from the collapsing local TV business than the NHL, NFL, and NBA. A 2023 Sportico report found that local media, including radio, accounts for 23% of MLB team revenue. With revenue from the regional sports network business drying up, MLB will have more incentive to maximize its national media rights revenue.

There are some clear risks for MLB if it goes down this path, however. By going to streaming, MLB would make its games less accessible and likely hurt its viewership, at least in the near term. The reach of broadcast television is still unmatched for live sports viewership, though streamers have closed the gap in recent years for major events like Netflix's Christmas Day games or Prime Video's Thursday Night Football.

There's also the PR nightmare moving the World Series to streaming would create. Whichever league moves its championship to a streamer first is going to have to put up with some very angry fans and some terrible press coverage. Polling shows that Americans are extremely unhappy with sports fragmentation, and that was with no league championships on streaming.

Not to mention, the federal government has taken interest in slowing the shift of live sports from broadcast to streaming. MLB, like other pro sports leagues, enjoys a federal antitrust exemption that could be put in jeopardy should the league make an aggressive move towards streaming.

So, there is no guarantee that either the NHL or MLB will move their championships to a streamer, even on a partial basis. The NHL may be wary because of its decision to split the Stanley Cup Final between over-the-air television (ABC) and cable (TNT) has not paid off from a viewership standpoint.

But with national media rights becoming even more important, and the World Series still holding incredible value, the league will at least consider selling it to a streamer, if only to test the market.

title: Apple TV content pipeline adds ‘F1 Academy’ and major scripted slate through early 2027
article_text:
Apple TV is bolstering its live sports and prestige scripted lineup heading into 2027, unveiling a new motorsport rights deal alongside premiere dates for several high-profile series.

On the sports front, Apple and Formula 1 announced that Apple TV will become the exclusive U.S. streaming home of “F1 Academy” beginning in 2027, coinciding with the all-female racing series’ fifth season. The deal expands Apple’s existing Formula 1 partnership and gives U.S. subscribers access to every qualifying session and race.

On the scripted side, Apple confirmed that Season 2 of the hit anthology legal thriller Presumed Innocent — now led and executive produced by Rachel Brosnahan and Matthew Rhys (Willow’s Bay) alongside Courtney B. Vance and Fiona Shaw — will premiere on February 19, 2027. That will be followed on April 16, 2027, by Wild Things, a seven-episode limited series starring Jude Law and Andrew Garfield as legendary Las Vegas entertainers Siegfried & Roy.

Before the new year begins, Apple will also debut Season 2 of Bill Lawrence’s Vince Vaughn-led comedy Bad Monkey on December 2, 2026.

MacDailyNews Note: Apple TV is available on the Apple TV app in over 100 countries and regions, on over 1 billion screens, including iPhone, iPad, Apple TV 4K, Apple Vision Pro, Mac, popular smart TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, VIZIO, TCL and others, Roku and Amazon Fire TV devices, Chromecast with Google TV, PlayStation and Xbox gaming consoles, and at tv.apple.com, for $14.99 per month with a seven-day free trial for new subscribers. For a limited time, customers who purchase and activate a new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV 4K or Mac can enjoy three months of Apple TV for free.

title: CAF turns profit of over $30m in 2025-26
article_text:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) governing body has recorded a profit of $31.2 million for the 2025-26 financial year.

This represents a welcome return to profitability for Egypt-based CAF, which managed this through increasing its total revenue to $284 million during the last financial year.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The governing body unveiled these figures at its 2026 general assembly in Nigeria, over the weekend.

CAF has turned its position around in the last half-decade – five years ago, it had debts of over $100 million.

This past year's figures were boosted by the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) men's national teams tournament in Morocco – over $100 million in revenue arrived through the continent's flagship event.

The soccer body's cash balance position has also improved – as of June this year, that figure came to $118.8 million.

CAF is now able to provide financial support to each of its member federations of $700,000, with this figure having most recently increased in July. Overall, the governing body has the eventual aim of taking this number up to the $1 million mark.

In terms of overall prize money and solidarity funding to African club soccer sides, meanwhile, CAF is this year contributing $48 million. In 2021, that same figure was only $19 million.

Prize money for national teams has also increased significantly over the last half-decade – the winners of the 2025 AFCON, for example, received $10 million, double what the 2021 AFCON winners were allocated.

For the Women's AFCON, the 2026 winners took home $2 million, up from just $200,000 five years ago.

In terms of recent CAF activity, earlier this month, the governing body unveiled a tie-up with sports data provider FeedConstruct.

Armenia-based FeedConstruct has snapped up exclusive match data and betting streaming rights to the full range of top-tier CAF competitions.

CAF is also looking for host nations for the next three editions of AFCON, due to be held in 2028, 2031, and 2033.

That process has a deadline of December 8 for the proper submission of all related documents and government guarantees by interested parties.

CAF, in addition, has a new secretary general, with Nigeria's Samson Adamu having recently been appointed.

title: TTFA explores development partnership with Aspire Academy
article_text:
In what is hoped will be a significant step towards advancing sporting development in Trinidad and Tobago, president of the Trinidad and Tobago Football Association (TTFA), Kieron Edwards, and Secretary of Youth Empowerment and Sport in the Tobago House of Assembly (THA), Assemblyman Keigon Denoon, are in Qatar holding high-level discussions with Ivan Bravo, Director General of the world-renowned Aspire Academy.

The discussions are focused on exploring strategic partnerships and major sporting development initiatives aimed at strengthening youth development, elite athlete training, coaching education, sports infrastructure and international opportunities for athletes across Trinidad and Tobago.

Aspire Academy, internationally recognised for its world-class sporting facilities, talent identification and athlete development programmes, represents a valuable potential partner in the continued transformation of the nation’s sporting landscape.

The engagement signals a shared commitment to move beyond traditional approaches to sporting development by pursuing international partnerships that can unlock opportunities, develop local talent and establish sustainable pathways to sporting excellence.

“Our ambition must be bigger than simply producing talented athletes. We must build the systems, partnerships and opportunities that allow our talent to compete and succeed on the world stage,” said Edwards.

Via a release yesterday, the TTFA said it views these discussions as an important step towards building a stronger sporting future for Trinidad and Tobago, with particular emphasis on empowering the next generation of athletes.

title: NFL exec: Streamers may be "more fan-friendly" option than ESPN
article_text:
In an interview last month that did not attract widespread notice until this past weekend, NFL VP/broadcast planning Mike North shed some light on the league’s thinking regarding streaming services.

Discussing a variety of schedule-related topics on the “It’s Always Gameday in Buffalo” podcast April 13, North confirmed the league will likely sell its new five-game media rights package to a streaming service, a move he characterized as increasing the availability of those games — most of which previously aired on ESPN as part of “Monday Night Football” doubleheaders.

“You’re going to move [the games] off of what amounted to ESPN only, which is down to 50 million homes,” North said. “If they end up on a YouTube, a Netflix, an Amazon, a streamer that’s arguably more widely distributed, you can make a case that it’s more fan-friendly. Everybody gets their paper towels from Amazon, everybody watches Netflix, and everybody can access YouTube for free, like they did last year with that Brazil game.”

The four ex-“MNF” games are being packaged with the league’s Week 1 International Series game from Australia in a bidding process that has reportedly included YouTube, Netflix and Fox Corporation. But North made clear that streamers are the favorite in the negotiation. “We’ll take those five games, probably deploy them in national windows, probably on a streaming partner,” he said.

The “Monday Night Football” doubleheaders typically featured one game on ABC and an overlapping game on ESPN, the latter of which usually attracted an unusually small audience. “Fans vote with their remotes, and they told us pretty clearly, two games on Monday wasn’t something that they were interested in,” North said, expressing some surprise that the doubleheader format did not resonate with viewers.

Technically, the doubleheader inventory Disney gave up as part of its NFL Network deal consisted of the three ABC-exclusive windows and one on ESPN+ (which last season was flexed to ESPN). But with ABC and ESPN simulcasting a single game in those weeks instead — as described by North in the interview — the change amounts to dropping four ESPN-exclusive editions of “MNF.”

It would be no surprise if the league sees streaming as a wider platform than cable. While the overwhelming majority of NFL game windows last season aired on broadcast television, the majority of non-broadcast windows aired on streaming services (21 across Amazon, Netflix and Peacock) rather than cable (15 across ESPN and NFL Network). The comments would likely have been regarded as conventional wisdom before the streaming backlash that has arisen in recent years, as the entire point of streaming was to eliminate the expense and inconvenience of cable.

Nevertheless, the comments provide some insight into the league’s media distribution strategy, and its approach to streaming, at a time when it faces federal scrutiny over its deals with streaming services.

It is worth wondering whether the league sees streaming as being more or less fan-friendly than broadcast television. North did not discuss broadcast in the context of the five-game package, except to say that if the league put the games “on a Sunday at 1:00, CBS and FOX [would be] grateful for the extra inventory, but most fans aren’t going to get to see those games.” But that would have to do more with the timeslot and regional format than the distribution method.

North’s 90-minute interview covered all manner of scheduling-related topics, including a potential delay to the annual schedule release due to negotiations over the five-game package and potential adjustments to the scheduling of Chiefs games due to Patrick Mahomes’ ACL injury.

Another notable item is that North did not rule out the league exercising its flexible scheduling option for holiday games on Christmas and Thanksgiving when asked directly about the possibility. The league’s Christmas Day slate last season featured games that looked strong on paper, but ended up pitting moribund teams. “Right now, we don’t contemplate flexing Thanksgiving and Christmas, but never say never. … I don’t think that’s something that we are actively contemplating right now, but give it another bummer Christmas like we had last year, and I’m sure the voices will get louder, and some voices carry more than others. And never say never.”

title: ‘This isn’t F1’: Max Verstappen criticises overtake-heavy Las Vegas Grand Prix
article_text:
Max Verstappen has said his outstanding victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday was not really true to the spirit of Formula One and how he wants to race.

Verstappen took a remarkable win, defending his lead and retaking it time and time again after it changed hands 35 times in a race dominated by the cars slipstreaming each other for 50 laps.

Verstappen vied with his Red Bull teammate, Isack Hadjar, Mercedes’s George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, and the McLaren of Lando Norris. Each time they would pass him he coolly came back at them to retake the lead.

It was an absorbing spectacle greeted with huge enthusiasm by the crowd in Las Vegas, and featured 352 overtakes across the field plus a gripping fight to the flag, where Verstappen won from Norris by six-tenths of a second.

The unusual racing, dominated by slipstreaming which has not been seen before to this extent in F1 in the modern era, was a result of the new regulations – including energy deployment and overtake modes – combined with the nature of the Las Vegas circuit, with its long straights and slow-speed corners.

Verstappen, who has been critical of the new regulations, obviously took great pleasure in a fine win but remained unconvinced that this was how F1 should be.

“For me personally this isn’t Formula One, the way that we are racing. It looks great on TV but this isn’t how it should be,” he said.

When asked if it was the kind of racing enjoyed, he was unequivocal. “When I look at it from my racer heart, no. When you look at it as a show spectacle, yes,” he added.

“I enjoyed my repassing and everything but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart. Even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because it just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably, yes, you like it.”

Early in the season as the teams came to grips with the energy deployment systems that produced what became known as yo-yo racing (frequent changes of position dictated by use of electrical energy) Verstappen and others unfavourably compared races to the video game Mario Kart. He returned to that comparison after Las Vegas, even while knowing it would probably not be well received by F1 management.

“I probably shouldn’t say it. I probably should not. I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart,” he said. “Sometimes you drop back and you get drafts and there’s a catch-up. Always when you’re dropping back, you go faster. So that’s the last time that I felt something like this.”

Slipstreaming was a regular part of F1 in the 1960s and 70s and prompted some of its most thrilling and revered races, not least the closest ever finish in 1971 when Peter Gethin won by one-hundredth of a second at Monza and there were six-tenths separating the top five.

There was nonetheless also considerable approval from across the paddock for this modern form of the discipline in Las Vegas, at very least in appreciation of how it had been embraced by the fans.

“From a racing point of view, from the outside, I’m sure it probably was the best race ever in Formula One,” said Lando Norris. “You never know what’s going to happen. There were overtakes out of nowhere. The thing is, sometimes you have a closing speed of 20-30km/h to people, especially to us and some of the overtakes weren’t overtakes, you press boost and you go past someone. But the racing was still good. You’re still fighting for position, and there are a lot of good things in there.”

The Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, said that the race may have divided opinion, especially from purists who dislike the artificial nature of the use of overtake mode and energy deployment, but noted that the F1 audience was now a broad church.

“I guess you will have many people that will say that’s not racing. Personally, we need to be open minded,” Wolff said. “Susie [Wolff’s wife] was in the paddock club and she said that for 90 minutes people were screaming with the overtakes. The instant feedback I got from the friends watching, our sponsors, was: ‘That was awesome.’ Stefano [Domenicali, F1 CEO] liked it very much. That’s not going to happen everywhere.”

title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Untelevised Ferrari team radio puts Leclerc and Vasseur in the firing line
article_text:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has revealed that Charles Leclerc was warned five corners before his collision with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, putting both the Monegasque driver and his boss under fresh scrutiny.

Vasseur admitted that Ferrari had already sent Leclerc a message about the situation just five corners before the collision took place on Lap 38, before going on to describe the subsequent incident as a "professional mistake".

The revelation raises uncomfortable questions for Leclerc, whose judgement has come under strong scrutiny, but also for Vasseur - who must now explain why Ferrari's warning failed to prevent the two team-mates from colliding.

Vasseur cut an increasingly frustrated figure in his post-race media interviews, describing the incident as "completely unacceptable".

Not only did it come just two weeks after he brokered crisis talks in Brazil which focused on Ferrari's drivers respecting their team, it came just seconds after yet another warning for Leclerc in an as-yet-untelevised team radio message.

Vasseur, speaking to F1's official channels, said: "Honestly, my position is that once again it's more than unacceptable. I had exactly the same word at Mexico - it's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, but mainly for the people working at home.

"We had a clear discussion after Mexico - I think I was quite harsh. We passed the message to Charles five corners before, and for me it's a professional mistake.

"I know that he apologised, I know he was sorry, but once again we destroyed the race today. We could have done much better."

This new revelation puts further focus on Leclerc and his apparent inability to adapt his approach when Ferrari's wider interests are at stake. For the second time in three races he was penalised for a highly ambitious move on his team-mate which came at major cost for all concerned.

As he had been in Mexico just three weeks ago, Leclerc was penalised by the stewards for his error, while Hamilton's race was compromised on both occasions. That is before considering the wider damage to Ferrari.

While driving an F1 car at around 200mph with precision around tight streets is a difficult job, this latest incident happened literally seconds after he had been warned.

It is a terrible look for the driver Ferrari have long viewed as a future world champion. The driver who just received a long-term contract extension.

While Vasseur's new revelation about that radio warning puts more pressure on Leclerc, it also inadvertently ramps up the heat on the 58-year-old Frenchman as well.

If Vasseur's crisis talks after Brazil, and a warning seconds before a collision, do not deliver the desired result, what does that say about the leadership at Ferrari?

Vasseur himself described the situation on track between the two drivers as "unmanageable" in the aftermath of Saturday night in Vegas. But what does that say about the man who is supposed to be managing it?

One thing is for sure - the Hamilton-Leclerc relationship will become an even bigger issue as time goes by, and the Scuderia to an extent asked for this problem when they hired both as 'number one drivers'.

Questions will inevitably be asked about whether the current arrangement can survive into 2027.

As he was in Mexico, Hamilton was the injured party here, with the FIA stewards confirming Leclerc's culpability by penalising him on both occasions. The seven-time world champion is also the man Ferrari brought in to help change the team's fortunes, swimming against the tide of its history.

What happens next for Leclerc and Vasseur?

All fingers right now point to Leclerc and Vasseur for this sorry Scuderia mess. Leclerc because all these words about 'respect' for the team appear to have made little difference. And Vasseur because his interventions have so far failed to prevent another incident.

Now all questions and focus will be on what Ferrari do next, and at some stage soon the team's leadership may need to make a decisive intervention.

One thing is for sure, the status quo is not working, and it will not work. Change is needed and it is needed fast.

Once again, the clock is ticking at Maranello.

title: F1’s $3.2 Billion Las Vegas Legacy Sets The Stage For Luxury Brands To Up Their Game In 2026
They Just Won the 2026 F1 Academy Championships. Alisha Palmowski, Rafaela Ferreira Talk Their Defining Season
article_text:
Alisha Palmowski and Rafaela Ferreira have learned how to stay calm under pressure, helping Campos Racing win the 2026 F1 Teams’ Championship.

The Red Bull Academy Programme drivers reflect on their successful second year in the all-female Formula 4–level racing series and tell TODAY.com their improved confidence and execution over the last year secured them the top honors.

“Being at both of our second years, I think we were both able to take a lot of learnings from last year and just execute it a little bit better,” 20-year-old Palmowski, who clinched the 2026 Drivers’ title, says. “I was much more confident going into this year, a lot calmer. Just knew more of what to expect of the whole procedure of F1 Academy. A completely different driver and person than the driver who turned up to Shanghai last year.”

Ferreira, 21, who came in 11th overall in the individual competition, described the season as “a little bit more challenging,” yet is “very happy” with how the year went.

In its fourth year, the F1 Academy’s 2026 season consisted of 14 races across six rounds. It kicked off in March in Shanghai and ended Nov. 21 in Las Vegas, coinciding with the Formula 1 Grand Prix. The Susie Wolff-led initiative is on a mission to help young women get involved in motorsport.

Below, Campos Racing’s Palmowski and Ferreira share their early racing memories, what they wish people knew about F1 Academy and more.

Alisha Palmowski: I’ve always been the biggest F1 fan ever since I was a really young child. For as long as I can remember, I always grew up with the influence of it on TV. The first time I experienced F1 cars in real life would have been Silverstone in 2015 at the British Grand Prix. I think I was about 8 or 9 years old at the time, and I think that’s where my passion for motorsport was really unlocked. The speed, the sound, the smell, everything. I just got hooked instantly.

Rafaela Ferreira: I remember my dad showing me some races from (Brazilian driver) Ayrton Senna. I think it was when I started to watch F1. I think the first time I went to a Grand Prix was four years ago ... I was racing in a support series and I went to the track as well. So I was racing at the same time I was watching F1 for the first time. I think I was more worried about watching F1 than racing my race.

What is one thing that you wish more people knew about F1 Academy? Something that might help another young girl who has hopes of making it where you are today?

AP: I think how tough this series is. I think it’s often underestimated. In F1 Academy, we’re obviously an F4 level series, but I think we have different challenges to what other F4 level series have. Racing as a support series to F1, the amount of track evolution that we have across a race weekend. When F1 go out, lay their rubber down, the adaptability that we need from session to session, it’s very high. I think that’s where it really differs from a standard F4 level series. But if you progress through the ranks up to F2 or F3, they experience the exact same thing. So it’s giving us a great foundation to learn those basics and to take forward. That’s probably what people don’t realize is, it’s tough, it’s very difficult.

RF: I think it’s how much we work behind the scenes. It seems as if it’s just like seven rounds, but in the end we have a lot of things to do. We have a lot of work on the (simulators). When I was racing before in F4, we didn’t have a lot of work on the sim. We would just go to the track, do a lot of laps on the training, and then you’re gonna see how it’s gonna be. But here we have a lot of work on the sim, something that we need to learn as well. It’s very important.

What is your defining moment for the 2026 F1 Academy season?

RF: Canada this year was a very good race. I led the race from the start from the pole. The weekend was very competitive for me. I love Canada. I love to race on that track, so it was a very good weekend.

AP: Austin, to be honest. Actually wrapping up the championship. It’s what we worked towards all year. And it was a very high-pressure weekend because although I had the buffer to second place, it was like the elephant in the room. I know everybody expected it and wanted it to happen, but nobody really wanted to say it. So I tried to approach it very much as a normal race weekend, but it was very obvious that it wasn’t a normal race weekend. When I got in the car, there were like 30 photographers around my car. So, just the fact that I was able to stay calm under that pressure, I think that was what I was most proud of this year.

title: Gatorade "Body of Science" Highlights Women's Research Gap with F1 ACADEMY at Las Vegas Grand Prix
Friday Night 5G Lights: 5 Takeaways From Our Sit-Down With T-Mobile’s Kaley Gagnon
article_text:
The business of youth sports, first in your search results.

T-Mobile’s Friday Night 5G Lights awarded more than $8.4 million to high schools in 2026, its third season, and more than $16 million since its 2024 launch, according to T-Mobile. YSBR sat down with Kaley Gagnon, Vice President of Marketing at T-Mobile, for an episode of the Jr. Sports Marketing podcast to talk about where the program came from and what it has done for the business.

We recorded before the 2026 field was cut to 40 Division Finalists. Since then, Menasha High School in Menasha, Wis., has won the $1 million grand prize, T-Mobile announced November 12.

Gagnon has spent nearly 20 years in telecom, she said, and joined T-Mobile about five years ago to launch and scale its 5G Home Internet product. She grew up an Air Force kid who moved often. The constant, in her words, was Friday night football, and the Airheads from the concession stand.

Here are five takeaways from our conversation.

1. T-Mobile’s Sports Strategy Starts With the Experience, Not the Logo

T-Mobile’s mission is to be the best in the world at connecting people to their world, Gagnon said, and few things are more central to people’s worlds than sports and entertainment. “It was less about, let’s put our logo and the color magenta on the back of the wall,” she said. “It was more about how do we make the experience better for consumers and for our members.”

She described three pillars. The first is the network inside the game. She cited Major League Baseball’s automated ball-strike system, where a tap of the helmet now signals a challenge, as an example of network integration changing how a sport is played.

The second is member perks. Club Magenta gives T-Mobile customers a place to rest, recharge and skip the line at events like Lollapalooza in Chicago. Gagnon called it “that little bit of pixie dust on top.”

The third is community, through programs like Friday Night 5G Lights and T-Mobile’s partnership with Little League, aimed at making youth sports more accessible.

2. Friday Night 5G Lights Started as a Small-Town Business Problem

Gagnon was direct about the origin. T-Mobile was growing nationally but finding growth harder in smaller towns, she said, even after millions of dollars in network investment and new stores in those markets.

The team called it a gap between perception and reality. “The perception was still maybe that T-Mobile wasn’t a brand in their community, wasn’t a brand that was going to work for them, even though the reality was there and the proof was there,” she said.

So the team went into those communities and talked with the mobile experts who staff T-Mobile stores there, looking for one thing every town shared that the company could invest in at scale. The answer came at the end of an afternoon conversation, when someone asked a rep about evening plans. The reply: the high school football game.

“That is where everybody comes together. It’s the social event of the week,” Gagnon said. “When we make a commitment, we don’t go small.”

3. How Does Friday Night 5G Lights Work?

Big sweepstakes can scare small communities off entirely, Gagnon said, because they assume they will never be the one. The first design principle was spreading the money. “We want a lot of communities and schools to benefit from this program,” she said.

The mechanic is apply, post, win. Every social post with the program’s hashtag, #FN5GL, counts as an entry into $5K Fridays, with winners drawn weekly. In 2026, 1,000 schools received $5,000 each, according to T-Mobile. “$5,000 goes such a long way in making a difference in these communities,” Gagnon said.

Public voting takes over from there. This season added four geographic divisions, which Gagnon compared to conference rivalries in college sports. T-Mobile narrowed more than 2,400 applications to 40 Division Finalists at $25,000 each, then to four Division Champions in the West, Midwest, South and East at $250,000 each, the company said. Those four competed for the $1 million field upgrade. Gagnon said there were 25 finalists in 2025.

Communities supply the rest. The 2025 champion, Dierks High School in Arkansas, won with nearly 2 million votes from a town of 884 people, according to T-Mobile. Gagnon said Dierks’ rival football team put the voting QR code on its jumbotron and took timeouts for voting, and 2024 winner Inola High School in Oklahoma sent supporters by bus to Tulsa to hand out QR codes.

4. Credibility First, Then Growth That Outlasts the Season

T-Mobile’s core product is reliability, Gagnon said, so credibility has to come before any pitch. “It’s very easy for big brands to come in with the blunt instrument and slap their logo everywhere and say, ‘We’re here, you’re welcome,'” she said. “That’s not our brand.”

She placed the program at the top of a traditional marketing funnel. “Before you start selling me on something, make me believe that it’s going to work for me and make me believe that you’re a brand that actually cares who I am in my community,” she said.

The program rarely talks about coverage, yet Gagnon said it has opened people’s minds to giving T-Mobile a look. In the communities T-Mobile tracked, deeper engagement, from $5K Fridays through the later rounds, lined up with more business growth, she said, “not just during the program, but over time after the program.” She did not share specific figures.

title: F1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix delivers nonstop action in another sellout
article_text:
The Las Vegas Grand Prix this past weekend was “a remarkable, breathless offering that saw positions changing multiple times on each lap” -- and was “very Indy 500-esque,” according to Chris Medland of RACER. Not only did the race place “a high demand on power unit deployment, but the tow -- and how to use it -- was a major factor in the outcome.” With a huge pack able to sit in behind the lead car, it “became about avoiding incidents, cleanly navigating the pit stop phase, and then timing your charge to the front.” It was a “unique race where drivers looked capable of climbing through even without a major pace advantage.” On some tracks earlier this F1 season, the layout “almost didn’t matter.” There would be “yo-yoing from the start that would settle down as the race wore on.” But in Las Vegas, there was “no such settling down.” The track layout, “energy challenges and powerful tow all combined with low-speed corners that were less problematic in terms of aerodynamic disruption when closely following another car ahead.” Most viewers of the Indy 500 would “call it an entertaining race regardless of the overriding need to just stay on the lead lap and be near the front for the final stages.” Las Vegas’ characteristics “delivered a challenge along the same lines, and we saw drivers having to think in a similar way to those who have had their eyes on the Borg Warner Trophy” (RACER, 11/22).

CHEF’S KISS: MOTORSPORT’s Filip Cleeren noted the race had 35 lead changes and “felt like the glitzy, battery-assisted street course version of the Indy 500.” It was “quite fitting to see how in America’s artificial entertainment capital, F1 put on an entertaining, if somewhat artificial, spectacle.” It may “not have been everyone’s cup of tea, but you’ll be hard-pressed to find anyone in attendance that didn’t feel like they got their hard-earned money’s worth” (MOTORSPORT, 11/22).

EYES ON FUTURE SUCCESS: In Las Vegas, Mick Akers noted the event again sold out, “leaving a hefty economic impact on Southern Nevada.” Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority President & CEO Steve Hill said that the three-day mega-event is “expected generate around” $800M -- “making it the biggest event of any year that a Super Bowl isn’t happening in Las Vegas.” MGM Resorts International CEO Bill Hornbuckle said that he is “pleased with how the event has evolved over its four years.” Hornbuckle added that MGM is “locked into hosting the Bellagio Fountain Club through at least 2034,” and he is “looking forward to more successful race weekends to come.” Las Vegas Grand Prix CEO Emily Prazer said that they “are going to improve the infrastructure needed to stage the race.” Upgrades at F1’s building include undergrounding utilities and building a permanent podium. Around the Strip, F1 is working with Clark County to be “able to add permanent fixtures around the circuit to speed up the set up and tear down of the race’s infrastructure” (LAS VEGAS REVIEW-JOURNAL, 11/22).

title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari’s top-speed deficit was “brutal” at F1 Las Vegas GP
article_text:
Ferrari Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton says the SF-26's top-speed deficit was exposed as even more "brutal" than he expected on Las Vegas' long straights.

Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were both eliminated in Q2 and finished the race down in seventh and 10th, with their potential squandered by a 10-second penalty for each – including one inflicted on Leclerc for colliding with his team-mate, which didn't help matters.

Ferrari's actual pace was better than in qualifying – they stayed within five seconds of the race leader for most of the race – but Hamilton felt their lack of straightline speed was costly as 'yo-yo' racing returned to F1.

"We knew that we have a pace deficit on the straights, but we weren't expecting it to be so brutal here with these long straights," the Briton commented.

"It was important always to make sure you're behind the car, and trying to move forwards you always have to make sure you're in a tow. Otherwise, you're just a sitting duck to people around.

"The Mercedes and the Red Bull, their power on a straight line is impressive. Really impressive.

"My engine was on the limit, there was nothing else coming out. I was pressing the button as hard as I could to make moves."

Hamilton's top speed in the race was 316.7km/h, interestingly 13.4km/h down on pacesetting Leclerc's 330.1km/h, while the top Mercedes and Red Bull were on 320.6km/h and 314.3km/h respectively.

"I've fought as hard as I can and given everything I could to get those points today. We were just constantly hit with challenges. I just kept my head down," the Ferrari driver added, before reacting to his penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

"Ten seconds was insane and very, very harsh," he reckoned. "I was avoiding colliding with the McLaren. They could have just told me to give the place back. Ten seconds to stop and go is nuts.

"But I came back and I got back into the fight and I could see Max up ahead." That's how decent Ferrari's pace was, but team principal Fred Vasseur was struggling to see any positives after his drivers collided yet again.

"I don't want to say that the pace was good or whatever, because for me today it's anecdotic," the Frenchman sternly commented. "For sure, when we came back and we overtook McLaren and so, I had a positive feeling. But honestly, it's not the topic on my desk."

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website.

title: Perez and Camara react to Las Vegas GP clash
article_text:
Sergio Perez's Las Vegas Grand Prix came to an early end when the Cadillac driver collided with the Haas of Rafael Camara.

Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara have each given their take on the moment they collided during the Las Vegas Grand Prix, an incident that saw Perez receive a grid penalty for next weekend’s race in Qatar.

The Cadillac driver had been attempting to overtake Camara on the approach to Turn 14 – as the race neared its halfway point – but made contact with the rear left tyre on the Haas, sending both cars into the barriers.

Camara was able to rejoin and finish the race while Perez found himself out of the running, with the Safety Car subsequently deployed. The stewards later found Perez at fault when the incident was investigated and handed him a five-place grid drop for the next event he participates in, that being the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix.

Reflecting on the clash after jumping out of the car, Perez explained: “I just spoke to Camara and he said that he didn't see me, because it's a bit weird – you exit Turn 12, like one second behind, which is a massive distance, and then you are halfway down the straight alongside.

“And unfortunately he didn’t see me so I was alongside him and, when I saw that he basically did the corner as if I wasn't there, and when I tried to avoid it, it was just too late.”

Despite the disappointing end to his race, the Mexican took heart from how the car had been performing prior to that.

“We were in the mix,” he added. “We stayed in racing with the Overtake Mode and we were fighting other cars, which was good. The race was going well up to that point.”

Camara, meanwhile, admitted that he needed more time to assess what had happened with Perez as he looked back on how his second F1 race had unfolded, having crossed the line in P16.

“I think at some parts it was quite fun,” the Brazilian said. “We had some overtakes and it's always nice to be battling, but in the end it was a bit more boring being alone the whole race, and then at the end I got overtook by Isack [Hadjar] and [Liam] Lawson.

“But no, I think it was positive race. I think also through the race I was always improving myself inside the car. I think the start was a bit tricky to get the tyres in temp and get a good first lap, but I think once we had everything under control, I think it was a decent race.

“Obviously there was the touch with Checo, but I still need to see what happened there exactly.”

It has since been confirmed that Camara will again race for Haas at the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix ahead of his full-time debut in 2027, but – speaking before this was announced – the 21-year-old conceded that the experience he had gained in Sao Paulo and Las Vegas had already proven beneficial.

“Everything that happened was very positive,” he explained. “I think it's very rare to get some laps before you start your full season with an F1 car doing the races.

“Obviously we have the testing, but a race weekend is always a bit different and I think that was very useful. And yeah, now we just need to see what will happen, and whatever happens we're going to be ready.”

title: A disappointed Arvid Lindblad reflects on the 'strangest thing' that ended his F1 Las Vegas GP
article_text:
A downcast Arvid Lindblad reflects on the moments before the spin that prematurely ended his superb run at the Formula 1 Las Vegas GP.

The rookie left Las Vegas disappointed after looking set for a potential personal best result. The Grand Prix in Sin City began on a bright note for Lindblad, who lined up fifth on the grid. His stunning performance saw him climb to third early on, with high potential for a great result.

However, a spin while attempting to get his cold tyres up to temperature on Lap 20 turned the day around. After the spin, the rookie was unable to get going again and was forced to retire. At the time of the spin, the Racing Bulls driver was running sixth.

Despite the incident being the “strangest thing” he has experienced, the 19-year-old still decided to admit fault for the spin.

“I honestly don’t know what happened,” Lindblad said to media, including Motorsport Week.

“I had a very bad shift, but in the end, it is still my fault; there is no point in blaming that, but it was a very strange feeling and something I’ve not really experienced in the car. I wasn’t doing anything strange; I was very slowly going on throttle, and then I was facing the wall.

“In the end, it’s my fault, and I’ll take it on the chin. But I can’t sit here now and say I understand why, because it was the strangest thing I’ve experienced.”

The night race in Sin City took viewers for a thrilling ride with 352 overtakes, setting the record for the most overtakes in a single F1 race. With the pack tightly bunched, the fight for position was nearly constant.

While he admits the race will be a “difficult one to swallow” because of the missed opportunity, Lindblad still took positives from the early stint. Speaking about the opening stage of the race, Lindblad reflected on the “fun” he had racing against the top teams.

“It was quite fun,” the Racing Bulls driver said. “It’s quite rare that you’re able to fight the top teams. I think it’s just very upsetting that we were in that position and it wasn’t able to capitalise on it.

“It’s going to be a difficult one to swallow because there really was something… I was fortunate to be in a position that we could earn something special today.

title: The 2027 cycling transfer market weakens Tadej Pogacar and several other top teams for one major reason
article_text:
In modern cycling, signing a star does not always guarantee the strongest team. Behind the victories of Tadej Pogacar, Remco Evenepoel and Jonas Vingegaard are riders who sacrifice their own chances to control races, make the mountains harder, protect their leaders and solve tactical problems.

That is why the 2027 transfer market could have significant consequences for some of the peloton’s biggest teams: several squads have lost support riders who may prove much harder to replace than expected.

UAE Team Emirates XRG and Red Bull - BORA - hansgrohe face significant departures, while Lidl-Trek and Decathlon CMA CGM are among the teams best placed to benefit from the moves. This is not simply a matter of changing names on a roster, but of shifting the balance of strength around the leading riders.

UAE has built one of cycling’s strongest squads, but it also needs to retain a collective structure capable of backing Pogačar throughout the season. In 2027, it will lose Pavel Sivakov, who is joining Decathlon CMA CGM, and Igor Arrieta, who will continue his career at Lidl-Trek.

Sivakov’s departure is particularly significant given his ability to work in the mountains. The Frenchman has been a valuable asset in Grand Tours and stage races, where he can raise the pace and support the leaders on demanding days. He does not have the profile of the team’s biggest stars, but his value lies precisely in being able to do that work without needing opportunities of his own.

Arrieta, meanwhile, is a more versatile rider with room to develop. His ability to perform across different terrain makes him useful in both one-day races and stage events. His departure also means losing a young option from a squad that needs depth to compete on several fronts.

UAE will bring in Marco Frigo, Abel Balderstone, Davide Stella and Pierre Gautherat, although they do not all match the profiles of the riders leaving the team. The key question is how the squad will reorganise its groups around Pogačar and its other leaders.

Red Bull - BORA - hansgrohe has strengthened its project with major leaders, but it also faces departures affecting several areas of the squad. Nico Denz is joining Tudor Pro Cycling, Jordi Meeus is moving to Lidl-Trek and Emil Herzog will continue his career at EF Education-EasyPost.

Of the three, Denz’s departure is particularly notable from a team-work perspective. The German is an experienced rider who can bring power on the flat, control breakaways and work for hours in support of his teammates. That kind of profile is vital in Grand Tours, especially when a team needs to control a stage or protect its leaders before the mountains.

Meeus has a different role, focused more on fast finishes, while Herzog represents a long-term investment. So, not every departure directly affects the support-rider group, but Red Bull-BORA must reorganise several areas of its squad.

The German team has enough resources to find alternatives, although collective performance depends on more than simply assembling quality riders. It also needs specialists who are willing to take a supporting role and know how to deliver at decisive moments.

Jordi Meeus will ride for Lidl-Trek next season.

Lidl-Trek stands out among the teams that could emerge stronger. The squad will sign Igor Arrieta, as well as Felix Gall, Gregor Mühlberger, Filippo Ganna and Jordi Meeus. The transfer activity strengthens its options across different terrain and gives it more ways to support Juan Ayuso and its other leaders.

Arrieta’s arrival could be particularly valuable because of his versatility, while Mühlberger will bring experience in the mountains. Ganna and Meeus, meanwhile, strengthen other areas of the squad. Lidl-Trek is not just adding big names, but riders who can perform complementary roles in different races.

Decathlon CMA CGM can also benefit from its rivals’ departures. Pavel Sivakov will be joined by Laurens De Plus, who is arriving from Netcompany INEOS.

Both bring experience and the ability to work in the mountains, two vital qualities for a team looking to strengthen its presence in Grand Tours.

The French team will also have Ben O'Connor and Olav Kooij, though their roles will differ. Sivakov and De Plus could be particularly important in building a support unit around the team’s general classification ambitions.

The 2027 transfer market once again shows that teams are not built solely around riders who raise their arms in victory. A star can decide a race with an attack, but needs teammates who have worked for hours to put them in the right position.

Sivakov’s departure forces UAE to reshape part of its climbing unit. Denz’s exit takes experience and power away from Red Bull-BORA, while Lidl-Trek and Decathlon have opportunities to strengthen their structures with riders capable of taking on collective responsibilities.

The big question is whether the new arrivals can make up for the losses. In an increasingly competitive peloton, the difference does not always come down to who has the best leader.

It also comes down to who has the best teammates to support them. And in 2027, some of the most important moves may be the ones that generate the fewest headlines.
